final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was provided. The Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly and, in substance, conceded the core audit concern: there is no admissible evidence that the material limitation affecting a named launch use case has been resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That concession makes the argument more precise, but it does not improve compliance status under the stated policy. A bounded aggregate-readiness rationale may describe operational readiness, yet the governing release predicate remains unmet. This is therefore still noncompliant, not compliant_with_caveats: caveats can narrow an overbroad claim, but they do not satisfy a mandatory unresolved disclosure or approval condition when the evidence for that condition is absent.
remaining_concerns: The supply-chain vendor screening segment still misses target by 1.4 percentage points and is named in two manufacturer rollout commitments, so the weakness remains material under the policy text.
There is still no admissible evidence of final legal clearance on whether the gap must be disclosed.
There is still no admissible evidence of a launch-facing disclosure artifact, approved risk acceptance, or remediation to target before launch.

Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness only; they do not satisfy the separate pre-launch policy requirement for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
The actor's narrowed framing preserves the unresolved compliance predicate rather than curing it, so caveating the certification packet is not enough for compliance.
